messages:
Rosa (sales): OmniCorp POC blocked: their app in one DMZ zone fails TLS to our private endpoint. They see cert subject 'corp-inspect.local' — looks like TLS inspection. Need quick unblock for tomorrow demo.

OmniCorp-Network: Confirmed. DMZ1 fails with cert mismatch, DMZ2 OK. curl from DMZ1:

OmniCorp-Network: ```curl -v https://private.redwood-omni.internal/ready
* Connected to private.redwood-omni.internal (10.9.9.9) port 443
* TLS alert, unknown CA
* SSL: certificate subject name 'corp-inspect.local' does not match target host name 'private.redwood-omni.internal'```

Vik (neteng): Sounds like their SSL Splitter/Appliance is doing MITM and not preserving SNI or using a cert SAN we trust. Two short-term routes: 1) they add our origin IP to a bypass list so traffic goes direct, 2) they trust the inspection CA on the client hosts. Which can we ask for?

OmniCorp-Network: Bypass list needs change control but okay for one IP for 24h. Trusting CA across hundreds of endpoints is not possible before tomorrow.

Ivy (solutions): We can spin a POC-only egress endpoint with a single IP that you add to the bypass list. We'll terminate TLS there with a cert matching private.redwood-omni.internal. That avoids changing their clients. If bypass isn't possible, fallback is to build a short-lived server image that disables OCSP stapling and returns smaller chains (reduces some failures).

Ben (infra): I'll provision a dedicated POC VIP: 203.0.114.99. We'll front with ALB and cert with correct SANs. provision-bot: queued create-poc-alb(203.0.114.99). ETA ~20m.

OmniCorp-Network: We'll open a bypass rule for 203.0.114.99/32 for 36 hours. Need a security note and rollback time.

Ivy (solutions): Security note: this bypass is limited to a single IP and a strict 36-hour window; we will remove the endpoint and revoke the cert after window. No change to production hosted zones. Rollback plan: we will notify and remove route + IP.

Rosa (sales): OmniCorp — please confirm when bypass is in place and we'll test. If anything else pops, we'll toggle to the OCSP-disabled server.

OmniCorp-Network: Rule applied. Testing now...

OmniCorp-Network: ```curl -v https://private.redwood-omni.internal/ready
* Connected to 203.0.114.99 (203.0.114.99) port 443
* TLS handshake complete
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{ "ready": true }```

Rosa (sales): Demo unblocked. Thanks team. We'll document the long-term fix (resolver associations + managed peering) in the follow-up ticket. :tada:
